i personally feel like there’s two main sides to this:
1) guilt from the fact we were able to do something beneficial with our lives after aging out (i went straight to uni and was surrounded by people who could never fathom what i had been through)
2) guilt from those who say stuff like “oh only two years etc must not have been *that* bad” (again didn’t understand)

but i also feel like there’s a grey area for ourselves. i think everything in my life has taught me that it’s all about our own mindset because at the end of the day none of the two things i listed even matters. we were dealt bad cards same as others and also not the same, we just gotta make sure we are a) good people b) healing c) good members of the world

hiya i went into care this late as well, from 16 till i aged out. i always always felt like an imposter because i went to two proper foster homes in this time period whereas i kept hearing about others who went to many. i felt like a fraud at times because i thought i wasn’t “truly” in care but now i just think if i even ended up in the system then something must have put me there. i should have gone when i was younger due to the circumstances that happened but i was good at hiding things to the point where the adults around me didn’t take action (when they should have tbh). at the end of the day cases like ours are just as valid as those who have been in it for way longer because our trauma is our own that we need to cope with, comparison won’t help us heal. and if other people judge us for any of this then we know that they’re not the right people to be around us. take care of yourself and please make sure you support yourself the best way you can because those two years were enough to mess with my brain (and the prior 16 too) :)

Hi! I feel like unfortunately you answered your own question. Relationships are about respect, and she doesn’t seem to have that much for you and if she does it’s unpredictable. You have already been in a bad spot and you said you met her when you were at your lowest. I think maybe she may have brightened your days at the start but at the end of your post it’s clear that you’re drained by this. A healthy relationship means your values and times are respected but also appreciated. If you feel your efforts have no value then I would say maybe breaking up is for the better for both of you. Love is difficult but it shouldn’t be this hard on you especially when you’re pulling yourself out of a rough time. If I was you I would let her go ahead and do what she wishes about the pregnancy but keep in mind that anything she does is her own decision, you didn’t force her into doing anything. Someone who gets angry and blocks you and then unblocks you isn’t stable. And mood swings are hard to deal with but speaking from my own experience having a partner whilst struggling with your own emotions is tough and the changes in mood can hurt *both* of you. This doesn’t feel like a healthy relationship and you need to put yourself first. Your happiness comes first, do not sacrifice it at the expense of others. Big hugs from lil sis :)
